d: The medieval castle of the old town. Inside is the Cyprus Medieval Museum. The story says Richard the Lionheart married Berengaria here in 1191.
The big cathedral of Limassol, built in the early 1900s, with its dome and bell tower right by the old town.
The old town's main mosque with its slim minaret, a short walk from the castle.
The old harbour of Limassol: fishing boats, a long pier, cafés and fish restaurants.
The modern marina with yachts, shops, restaurants and houses on little islands in the sea.
The seaside park and promenade: palm trees, lawns, sculptures, a cycle path and the long Molos pier.
An old carob mill next to the castle, now a museum, restaurants and an events centre.
The restored old covered market in the heart of the old town.
A lively old-town square full of bars and cafés, right next to the market.
The classical Town Hall of Limassol with its garden.
Iroon Square: an old-town square with bars, music and restaurants.
The municipal theatre of Limassol, for plays, music and shows.
The Cyprus University of Technology has its buildings all around the old town.
An old shady park with big trees, and the small city zoo.
Finds from ancient Limassol district, beside the Municipal Garden.
A long green park that follows the Garyllis river through the city.
About 170 metres tall: the tallest building in Cyprus, right on the seafront.
The big football stadium of Limassol.
A sandy beach with a pine wood park behind it.
The old village up the hill, above the hotels of the tourist area.
A beach in the hotel area east of the city.
Ruins of Amathus, one of the old city-kingdoms of Cyprus, by the sea east of Limassol.
A village on the hill east of the city, with views over the whole bay.
